record it as such.","Strategy: net Sharpe on dev below the 60/40 SPY/IEF Sharpe + 0.10, or bootstrap bound of the Sharpe difference at or below zero.","Robustness: fewer than 75 % of the tilt/offset neighbors (tilt 0.2 or 0.4, offset -1 or +1) beat 60/40, or the strategy no longer beats 60/40 at doubled costs.","Publication decay: excess Sharpe over 60/40 after 2019 below half of the pre-2019 excess (G2 check)."],"family":"macro-announcement-premium","holding_period":{"rebalance":"weekly","typical_days":5},"market_exposure":"long_only","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Investors who rebalance or de-risk on a calendar unrelated to the Fed's communication rhythm (monthly balanced funds, risk-parity and volatility-target books that hold constant equity weights through the cycle), and investors who sell equities in odd weeks after weakness, before the dovish news arrives, and so sell the equity premium to holders who time the cycle.","why":"Cieslak, Morse and Vissing-Jorgensen (2019) document that the US equity premium is earned in the even weeks of FOMC cycle time (weeks 0, 2, 4, 6 counted from the last scheduled FOMC statement), while odd weeks earn about nothing. The signal comes from the monetary-policy schedule (the Fed's calendar, a money-market event clock) and the trade is in another market: equities against intermediate Treasuries. Monetary-policy news arrives in a biweekly rhythm, so the price of risk falls in those weeks and equity holders are paid for carrying policy uncertainty into them.","why_not_arbitraged":"The tilt adds equity risk exactly in the weeks when news is expected; the gain per week is small relative to weekly equity volatility (Sharpe of a single week pattern is low), so a leveraged arbitrageur faces large tracking risk for a modest edge. No event for week none. Only SPY is ever marked; IEF, TLT, SHY and LQD are always unmarked peers, so the abnormal return is SPY minus the mean of the four bond ETFs from the next open to the close five sessions later. The claim: SPY beats bonds in even weeks and lags them in odd weeks, more than at time-shifted placebo phases of the same event set.","horizons":[1,2,3,5,10],"primary_horizon_days":5},"notes":"Brief fit: the brief asks for a cross-asset 1-5 day idea. Pure daily lead-lag between markets is dead in this lab (mrel scan, H-0013, H-0040), and FRED market series arrive with a one-day lag (clock next_morning), so a fast information spillover cannot be traded at the next open. The closest fit with a real mechanism is a signal from the monetary-policy side (the Fed's pre-announced FOMC schedule, a money-market event clock) traded across asset classes (equities against Treasuries) at a weekly horizon. Family: filed under macro-announcement-premium (H-0042) on purpose. The mechanism is related but not identical: H-0042 tested the risk premium on the scheduled announcement sessions themselves (and found it confined to the announcement session, not kept at 3-5 sessions); this card claims a biweekly rhythm of informal Fed news over the whole cycle, with weeks 2, 4 and 6 far from any scheduled release. Week 0 overlaps H-0042's FOMC events; the third falsification criterion says how to read it if the effect sits only there. Reusing the family keeps the trial count honest. Design follows K-0005 and K-0027: an always-invested 60/40 book with a symmetric tilt, so average equity weight stays near the benchmark (slightly above, because even weeks are more frequent than odd ones; about 0.63 at tilt 0.3), and the mechanism test marks both even (+1) and odd (-1) weeks so generic equity-over-bond drift largely cancels and the placebo measures the phase of the cycle, not equity drift (the H-0041 and H-0042 caveat). Events: about 6-7 week starts per cycle, 8 cycles a year, 2002-08 to 2020 (IEF, TLT, SHY, LQD start 2002-07-30) gives roughly 900-1000 events on as many dates, so power is not the problem of H-0017. Costs: every week boundary moves 2 x tilt of the book between SPY and IEF (1.2 of notional per boundary at tilt 0.3, about 55 boundaries a year), in the two most liquid ETFs of their class. Expected gross per boundary is tilt x the even-odd spread of SPY minus IEF; it survives doubled costs only if the spread is several basis points per week above the SPY+IEF round trip. That is the most likely way the strategy dies even if the mechanism passes. Expected decay (K-0060): the latest third is a declared kill condition. Holdout 2021-2026 is untouched by this card, but the paper's sample (1994-2016) overlaps most of dev, so a dev pass is partly in-sample for the literature; the +20 literature trials and the post-2019 decay check account for that. ETFs have no forward source yet (K-0014): at most G4. Point-in-time: the FOMC schedule is published a year or more ahead; the dataset lists only scheduled meetings (unscheduled calls excluded, as in the paper). Cycle weeks are counted with past statement days and the pre-announced next date only.","references":[{"cite":"Cieslak, Morse, Vissing-Jorgensen (2019) Stock Returns over the FOMC Cycle, Journal of Finance 74(5)","year":2019}],"signal":{"description":"Inputs: macro_release_calendar_1d key next_fomc_sessions (XNYS sessions from day d to the next scheduled FOMC statement day strictly after d; known at the close of d), and SPY/IEF total returns from sharadar_sfp. Step 1 (FOMC days, past information only): session d is an FOMC statement day if next_fomc_sessions on the previous session equals 1. Let k(d) = number of sessions since the most recent FOMC statement day (k = 0 on the statement day). Step 2 (cycle week of session d, Cieslak-Morse- Vissing-Jorgensen definition, sessions = trading days): if next_fomc_sessions(d) == 1 (d is the session before a statement day), week = 0; else if 0 <= k <= 3, week = 0; else if 4 <= k <= 33, week = 1 + floor((k - 4) / 5) (so weeks 1..6); else (k >= 34, unusually long cycles) week = none. Sessions before the first FOMC statement day in the data have week = none. Step 3 (offset): the target for session d+1 uses week(d + 1 + offset_sessions) computed from the schedule; because next_fomc_sessions is a pre-announced schedule, the Builder must compute it from values known at the close of d only (for a session ahead, use next_fomc_sessions(d) to know whether d+1 is day -1 or the statement day, and k(d)+1 for counting forward; never read a future row). Step 4 (weights for session d+1, decided after the close of d and traded at the open of d+1): even week (0, 2, 4, 6): SPY = 0.6 + tilt, IEF = 0.4 - tilt; odd week (1, 3, 5): SPY = 0.6 - tilt, IEF = 0.4 + tilt; week none: SPY 0.6, IEF 0.4. TLT, SHY and LQD are never held (weight 0; they are only unmarked peers of the mechanism test). Orders are sent only on sessions where the target changes (week boundaries); between boundaries the book holds its target weights (no other trading). If SPY or IEF has no bar on a day, keep the previous weights. Fail loudly if next_fomc_sessions is missing for a dev session after the first valid value.","params":{"offset_sessions":{"grid":[-1,0,1],"value":0},"tilt":{"grid":[0.2,0.3,0.4],"value":0.3}},"timeframes":["1d","1w"]},"title":"FOMC-cycle equity tilt - 60/40 SPY/IEF book overweight SPY in even weeks and underweight in odd weeks of FOMC cycle time, weekly switches","universe":{"instruments":["SPY","IEF","TLT","SHY","LQD"],"kind":"instruments"}}

title: Threshold-rebalancing pressure - when a simulated 60/40 SPY/IEF book drifts past its band, tilt a 60/40 book against the rebalancers' next-session trade for one session
card_json: {"asset_classes":["us_etf"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"sharadar_sfp","fields":["ret_co","ret_oc"],"frequency":"1d","instruments":["SPY","IEF","VTI","DIA","IWM","TLT","AGG","SHY"],"period":["2003-10-01","2020-12-31"]}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: the one-session side-adjusted abnormal return of the marked equity ETFs against the bond peers is at or below the 95th percentile of the time-shifted placebos, or gross per event is below the round-trip cost.","Mechanism: the latest third of dev has the wrong sign (equities do not move against the rebalancers' trade in the most recent years).","Mechanism shape: the descriptive 5- and 10-session abnormal returns are larger than the 1-session one in the same direction. That would be slow drift or momentum, not a transient flow concession that reverts within about two weeks.","Strategy: net Sharpe on dev below 60/40 SPY/IEF + 0.10, or the bootstrap bound of the Sharpe difference is at or below zero.","Robustness: fewer than 75 % of the threshold_pp / tilt neighbours (0.5 and 2.0; 0.2 and 0.6) beat the 60/40 benchmark, or the result does not beat 60/40 at doubled costs."],"family":"rebalancing-flow-pressure","holding_period":{"rebalance":"daily","typical_days":1},"market_exposure":"long_only","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Mandate-driven rebalancers that trade a mechanical size on a mechanical date regardless of price and demand liquidity on the session after a band breach. They accept the concession because tracking their policy weights matters more to them than one day of execution cost.","why":"Large balanced investors (defined-benefit pensions, target-date and balanced funds, endowments) hold fixed stock/bond targets and many rebalance by a threshold rule: when the equity weight drifts more than a band away from target, they sell the asset that outperformed and buy the one that lagged, usually in index futures and ETFs on the next session. The trigger depends on the joint path of two markets: a bond selloff with flat equities pushes the equity weight up and causes equity selling just like an equity rally does, so the signal for the equity trade comes partly from the bond market. Harvey, Mazzoleni and Melone (2025) simulate 60/40 books with threshold and calendar rules and find that an overweight in equities predicts lower next-day equity returns and higher bond returns, with the pressure reverting within about two weeks. That is the signature of a non-informational flow that pays a temporary price concession.","why_not_arbitraged":"The aggregate band breach is not observed: each institution has a private band and anchor date, so the trigger can only be estimated. The concession is small next to one day of index volatility, so a liquidity provider earns a thin reward per unit of risk. Daily index-level capital is limited on stress days, when breaches cluster. The evidence was published only in 2025, after the whole dev period."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"After the close of day t, the simulated 60/40 SPY/IEF threshold book (primary threshold_pp = 1.0, rules exactly as in signal.description, including the reset) breaches its band. On such a day mark the four broad US equity ETFs SPY, VTI, DIA and IWM with side = -1 if equities are overweight (d_t = +1) and side = +1 if underweight (d_t = -1). Do not mark TLT, IEF, AGG or SHY: they are the unmarked bond peers, so the abnormal return is equity minus Treasury and aggregate bonds. This is the rebalancers' trade: equities should underperform bonds on the session after an overweight breach and outperform after an underweight breach. Both directions are marked so that generic equity-over-bond drift cancels in the placebo.","horizons":[1,2,3,5,10],"primary_horizon_days":1},"notes":"Brief fit: the brief asks for a short (1-5 day), cross-asset idea in which signals from one market trade in another. Here the trigger comes from the joint stock/bond path: a bond selloff alone can force equity selling, and the trade is in both markets. Instruments are the most liquid ETFs, so a one-session hold is affordable. This is the closest fit with a mandated-flow counterparty (K-0024: flow events are what survives in this lab); pure daily lead-lag between markets is dead (study mrel), so this card is deliberately not a lead-lag rule. Family: rebalancing-flow-pressure, reused honestly. Difference from H-0002: H-0002 used the calendar (month-end window, month-to-date drift sign, half-weight spread held over several days, flat otherwise). This card uses threshold breaches on any date, a one-session hold, and a tilt on an always-invested 60/40 book with the benchmark's average exposure (K-0005, K-0027). It answers H-0002's open question: does the next-day pressure exist at all, separately from a multi-day window? H-0044 (month-end FX hedging) is a different flow in the same family. Difference from H-0041 (flight-to-safety rebound, short-term-reversal): both directions are marked, and overweight breaches follow equity rallies or bond selloffs, which no stress-rebound story covers. Known confound, cannot be separated with a single event mask: a generic one-day reversal of the stock-minus-bond spread after large relative moves predicts the same sign. Only the absolute equity move after bond-driven breaches would separate the two, and the gate cannot report that split. If the mechanism passes, a follow-up control card (large relative moves that do not breach the band) is the natural next step. Expected gross against cost (K-0053): the paper reports roughly 17 bps lower next-day equity returns (futures, close to close). The engine fills at the next open, so the overnight part is lost; I expect perhaps half of it open-to-close, about 8-10 bps of equity-minus-bond abnormal return per event. Cost is a few bps per side on SPY/VTI/DIA/IWM, so the cost ratio may be only modestly above one. That is a stated risk. Event count: a 1 pp band breaks after roughly a 4 % relative move since the last reset. With a daily stock-bond spread volatility of about 1.4 %, I expect a few hundred breach dates in 2003-2020, times four marked ETFs. That is enough for min_events and min_event_dates. The 2.0 pp neighbour has about a quarter of the breaches, so it is the power-limited neighbour. Path dependence: the simulated book's anchor is the first loaded session, so a different start date shifts the breach dates. That is inherent to threshold rules (real institutions have heterogeneous anchors) and is deterministic for a given data start. Timing caveat: the event study measures open(t+1) to close(t+1); the strategy holds from open(t+1) to open(t+2), so it also carries the next overnight, where part of the reversal may sit. Period starts 2003-10-01 because AGG starts 2003-09-29; every other instrument exists earlier. No forward data for ETFs, so G4 is the ceiling (K-0014). The publication year (2025) is outside dev, so the publication-decay check does not apply in dev; the holdout includes the publication year.","references":[{"cite":"Harvey, C. R., Mazzoleni, M. G., Melone, A. (2025) The Unintended Consequences of Rebalancing. NBER Working Paper 33554","url":"https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w33554/w33554.pdf","year":2025}],"signal":{"description":"Inputs: daily close-to-close total returns of SPY and IEF, built from the sharadar_sfp return fields ((1 + ret_co) * (1 + ret_oc) - 1, or a close-to-close total return field if the loader provides one). Simulated rebalancer book: on the first session of the loaded period both legs start at weights 0.60 (SPY) and 0.40 (IEF), with growth factors G_s = G_b = 1. After each close t, multiply G_s by (1 + r_SPY,t) and G_b by (1 + r_IEF,t), then compute the equity weight w_t = 0.6 G_s / (0.6 G_s + 0.4 G_b). If SPY or IEF has no bar on day t, its return counts as 0 for the drift and no trigger can fire on t. Trigger: if w_t > 0.60 + threshold_pp / 100, then d_t = +1 (equities overweight, rebalancers sell equities and buy bonds on t+1). If w_t < 0.60 - threshold_pp / 100, then d_t = -1 (equities underweight). Otherwise d_t = 0. On a trigger day, reset G_s = G_b = 1 after the close of t, because the simulated rebalancer is back at target. Only data up to the close of t is used. Book (long-only, fully invested, only SPY and IEF are ever traded): the default target is SPY 0.60 / IEF 0.40. If d_t != 0, the target for session t+1 is SPY = clip(0.60 - tilt * d_t, 0, 1) and IEF = 1 - SPY, traded at the open of t+1. After the close of t+1 the target goes back to 60/40 (traded at the open of t+2), unless a new trigger fired on t+1, in which case the new tilt applies. Hold length is one session by design (the paper's pressure is a next-day effect) and is not a parameter. Outside tilts, hold constant 60/40 target weights. If the engine re-equalises target weights every day, that is acceptable (tiny turnover). Otherwise re-set to 60/40 at the first session of each month, like the benchmark. VTI, DIA, IWM, TLT, AGG and SHY are in the universe only as event instruments and peers for the mechanism test; the strategy never trades them.","params":{"threshold_pp":{"grid":[0.5,1.0,2.0],"value":1.0},"tilt":{"grid":[0.2,0.4,0.6],"value":0.4}},"timeframes":["1d"]},"title":"Threshold-rebalancing pressure - when a simulated 60/40 SPY/IEF book drifts past its band, tilt a 60/40 book against the rebalancers' next-session trade for one session","universe":{"instruments":["SPY","IEF","VTI","DIA","IWM","TLT","AGG","SHY"],"kind":"instruments"}}

title: Post-macro-release drift across asset classes - on CPI, payrolls and FOMC days, long the ETFs with the largest vol-standardized reaction and short the smallest, hold 5 sessions, dollar-neutral
card_json: {"asset_classes":["us_etf","macro"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"sharadar_sfp","fields":["ret_co","ret_oc","tradable"],"frequency":"1d","period":["2002-07-30","2026-09-25"]},{"dataset":"macro_release_calendar_1d","fields":["next_release_sessions"],"frequency":"1d"}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: the side-adjusted 5-session abnormal return of the release-day events is not above the 95th percentile of the time-shifted placebos.","Mechanism: gross abnormal return per event at 5 sessions is below the round-trip cost of the marked ETFs.","Mechanism: the 5-session abnormal return has the wrong sign in two of three dev sub-periods, or is negative in the latest third (decay kill condition, K-0060).","Mechanism shape: the 1-session abnormal return is positive but the 5- and 10-session returns are not larger (a quick partial move that is not the slow continuation the mechanism claims), or the 5-session sign is negative (release moves reverse: overreaction, not slow-moving capital).","Strategy: net Sharpe on dev below 0.5 against T-bills, or the bootstrap bound of the Sharpe difference to T-bills at or below zero.","Robustness: fewer than 75 % of the neighbours (top_k 2 or 4, hold_days 3 or 7) beat the T-bill bar, or net Sharpe at doubled costs falls below the bar.","Concentration: one dev third carries more than 60 % of the log return (for example only the 2008 crisis releases)."],"family":"post-macro-announcement-drift","holding_period":{"rebalance":"event","typical_days":5},"market_exposure":"market_neutral","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Slow allocators who trade on the release news days later: retail bond and equity fund investors whose flows follow realized performance, allocation committees and rebalancers, and intermediaries who faded the first move and unwind it. They pay the continuation to whoever positions on the release-day close.","why":"Scheduled US macro releases (CPI, the Employment Situation report, FOMC statements) are the main dated news events for whole asset classes, and they move them a lot on the day. Much of the capital that ends up absorbing that news moves slowly. Bond and equity fund investors react to the realized move with a lag of days to weeks. Brooks, Katz and Lustig document that fund outflows after rate increases gradually add supply, so long Treasury yields keep drifting in the direction of the FOMC surprise long after the announcement day. Multi-asset allocators rebalance on weekly or monthly committee schedules, and dealers who took the first order flow lay off inventory over several days. With slow-moving capital (Duffie 2010), the release-day move is only the first part of the adjustment: the asset classes that moved most on the release day (vol-standardized, relative to the others) should keep outperforming the ones that moved least over the following week, as the delayed allocation flows arrive. The signal comes from the macro calendar and from the cross-asset reaction it causes, and the trade is in the asset-class ETFs.","why_not_arbitraged":"Positioning across asset classes after a macro release means carrying large macro risk for a small expected gain per event, about 30 events a year with a low Sharpe per event. Macro funds' capital is limited and drawdown-constrained, and mutual funds cannot front-run their own investors' flows. The effect is spread over many asset classes and several days, so no single desk is set up to harvest it."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"On each scheduled US macro release session t (CPI, Employment Situation or scheduled FOMC statement day, known from next_release_sessions at the close of t-1 equal to 1), after the close of t: among the eligible universe ETFs, the top_k (=3) with the highest vol-standardized same-day return z = r_t / sigma_63 are marked with side +1 and the bottom_k (=3) with the lowest z with side -1. The other eligible ETFs on that date are unmarked and serve as peers (at least 3 by construction; dates with fewer eligible ETFs are not events). The mechanism says marked +1 ETFs outperform and -1 ETFs underperform the peers from the next open over the following sessions.","horizons":[1,3,5,10],"primary_horizon_days":5},"notes":"Brief: short horizon, cross-asset. The signal comes from the macro calendar (BLS and Fed schedules) and from the cross-asset reaction to the release, and the trade is a cross-section of 19 asset-class ETFs (equity regions, rate- and credit-sensitive sectors, Treasuries, credit, TIPS, metals, commodities, currencies). Family: a new name, post-macro-announcement-drift. It shares the release calendar with macro-announcement-premium (H-0042, H-0045) but makes a different claim. Those cards tested an unconditional premium of high beta or equity over bonds on or around release days, the same side every time. This card has no fixed side: its direction comes from each asset's own release-day reaction, and the claim is continuation (underreaction / slow-moving capital), not risk compensation. Its mechanism class is the one behind the lab's strongest mechanism result, the release-session reaction drift in stocks (K-0046), here applied to macro news and asset classes. If the Chair thinks it belongs in macro-announcement-premium or post-earnings-announcement-drift for trial counting, I accept that. Placebo: shifting the event set in time breaks the link between side and reaction, so the placebo mean should be near zero. Generic asset-class momentum would also lift the placebo, which makes the test stricter. Generic continuation after any large day (not only release days) is not separated by this test. The lab's daily lead-lag and autocorrelation scan (study mrel) found no such continuation in liquid ETFs, which is why the claim is tied to dated release news. Why this is not a stress rebound (K-0056): the side is continuation, not reversal. If stress-period releases reverse, the card dies on the sub-period or sign criteria, and that is informative. Expected size against the bar (K-0053, K-0064): about 30 release days a year (some coincide), and with 5-session holds the book is invested roughly 55-65 % of sessions. Turnover is about 60x gross a year. At liquid-ETF tiers that costs roughly 1.5-2 % a year, 3-4 % at doubled costs. The book's volatility when invested should be about 8-10 % a year, so a net Sharpe of 0.5 needs a gross relative return of about 20 bps per cohort per 5 sessions (about 6 % a year gross). By Brooks-Katz-Lustig's size estimates, a Treasury drift of a few bp of yield over a week is 20-50 bps on TLT, so the bar is within reach only if drift also shows up outside the bond ETFs. Weights: inverse-vol with a 0.25 cap so that low-vol ETFs (TIP, LQD, FXE, FXY) do not dominate. The sentinel limit per instrument is also 0.25. Point in time: the calendar dataset uses realized release dates. For the 2013 shutdown, the postponed CPI and jobs dates were not known in advance (catalog known_biases), a handful of events. Releases on NYSE holidays are counted on the next session by the dataset. All ETFs existed in dev: TLT and LQD from 2002-07, TIP 2003-12, EEM 2003-04, GLD 2004-11, FXE 2005-12, DBC 2006-02, SLV 2006-04, FXY 2007-02, UUP 2007-03, HYG 2007-04. Instruments join the ranking once they have 63 sessions of history, so the early cross-section has about 11-13 ETFs and always at least 3 unmarked peers (K-0055). No ICE BofA FRED series are used (H-0043 found them empty). ETFs have no forward data, so G4 is the ceiling.","references":[{"cite":"Brooks, Katz, Lustig (2018) Post-FOMC Announcement Drift in U.S. Bond Markets, NBER Working Paper 25127","url":"https://www.nber.org/papers/w25127","year":2018},{"cite":"Duffie (2010) Presidential Address: Asset Price Dynamics with Slow-Moving Capital, Journal of Finance","year":2010}],"signal":{"description":"Inputs: daily total returns of the 19 ETFs (close-to-close return of session t = (1 + ret_co) * (1 + ret_oc) - 1, where ret_co is the close t-1 to open t return and ret_oc the open t to close t return) and the macro_release_calendar_1d key next_release_sessions. Release day: session t is a release day when next_release_sessions observed at the close of session t-1 equals 1 (the next CPI, Employment Situation or scheduled FOMC statement day is session t). The schedules are published in advance, so this is known at the close of t-1. Eligibility on release day t: an ETF is eligible if it has a valid close-to-close return on t and at least 63 valid daily returns in the sessions t-63 .. t-1. ETFs not yet listed or without data are ignored. Reaction score: z_j = r_j,t / sigma_j, where sigma_j is the standard deviation of the ETF's daily close-to-close returns over sessions t-63 .. t-1 (the 63-day window is fixed, not a parameter). Cohort: after the close of each release day t, rank the eligible ETFs by z_j. Long leg = the top_k ETFs, short leg = the bottom_k ETFs. If fewer than 2 * top_k + 3 ETFs are eligible, no cohort is formed that day. Weights inside each leg are inverse-volatility: w_j = 0.5 * (1 / sigma_j) / sum over the leg of (1 / sigma), positive for the long leg and negative for the short leg. Each weight is capped at 0.25 in absolute value and the capped excess stays in cash (not redistributed). A cohort has gross 1 or less and is dollar-neutral up to the cap. Holding: a cohort is entered at the open of session t+1 and held for hold_days sessions; it expires after the close of session t+hold_days and is exited at the next open. The book on any day is the simple average of the target weights of all cohorts active that day (an expired cohort drops out; with no active cohort the book is flat in cash). Netting across cohorts is allowed, so gross stays at or below 1. Weights are recomputed only when a cohort starts or expires (no daily drift re-equalising in between). title: Month-end Treasury index-extension tilt - 60/40 SPY/IEF book that holds its bond sleeve in TLT instead of IEF over the last 2 sessions of each month

title: Flushed vs unflushed crashes in crypto perps - after a large bottom-tercile daily drop, long coins whose perp funding collapsed, short coins whose funding held, BTC/ETH hedged, hold 3 days

(1) Forced deleveraging: leveraged perp longs get liquidated and stop-run, perps trade below the spot index during the day, so the day's funding falls to a new weekly low and turns negative. The selling is non-informational and mechanically forced, so the price is pushed below value and partly recovers over the next days as liquidity providers are paid for absorbing it (Campbell, Grossman and Wang 1993: non-informational, liquidity-driven moves reverse, informational ones do not; Brunnermeier and Pedersen 2009: margin-driven liquidity spirals overshoot and then revert). (2) A crash during which funding did not fall: perp longs were not flushed (they held or added into the decline) and the selling came from spot or news (unlocks, delistings, hacks, project news). That move is informational, and the leverage that is still open is an overhang that gets liquidated later, so the coin should keep underperforming. The claim is the contrast: among same-day relative losers of similar size, flushed coins outperform unflushed ones over the next 1-5 days. Signal market: the funding (leverage-financing) market of the perps; traded market: the perp price.","why_not_arbitraged":"Absorbing a liquidation cascade means buying a falling, high-volatility asset while the venue's risk engine is still selling, which needs balance sheet exactly when market makers widen quotes and cut inventory (crypto market makers are thinly capitalised and themselves face margin calls). The rebound is uncertain in timing and the next leg of a cascade can go deeper, so capital that could take the trade is scarce at the moment. The short leg is an alt-perp short with squeeze risk. Capacity in alt perps is small, so large arbitrageurs ignore it."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"After the close of day t, a top-30 perp (not BTC or ETH) whose day-t return is in the bottom third of the universe and at or below -k_sigma times its own 30-day daily volatility. Abnormal return against the unmarked perps of the same date (at least the top two thirds of the universe stay unmarked).","horizons":[1,3,5,10],"primary_horizon_days":3},"notes":"Brief fit: the brief asks for a 1-5 day cross-asset card. The signal comes from the leverage-financing market of the perps (funding) and the trade is in the perp price; the cards' crypto_perp class covers both, so this is cross-market rather than cross-asset-class. I chose it over a US ETF / FRED idea on purpose: (1) fills at the next open kill cross-time-zone ideas (country ETFs, home-market reopenings), because the home market trades before the US open; (2) the owner's daily lead-lag scan (mrel, 706k tests) killed linear cross-market prediction among ETFs, FX, macro and crypto; (3) mixing FRED/ETF signals (holdout 2021) with crypto trades would probably cut crypto dev at 2020-12-31 and leave about three years of 2017-2020 crypto; (4) the ICE BofA credit series on FRED appear to have only recent history (likely cause of H-0043's zero events), so I avoid them. Relation to earlier cards: this is the event study H-0006 asked for (\"after extreme drops, do forward returns differ by falling funding versus not?\"), filed in H-0006's family short-term-reversal so the trials count together. Differences from H-0006: both sides are marked (flushed long, unflushed short), so generic reversal and the market bounce after stress (K-0056, studies 6-7) cancel in the contrast and the placebo mean should be near zero; no BTC trend gate; abnormal return against same-date unmarked perps, so a persistent market-wide crash does not drive the result (K-0056 asks how a design separates a one-off shock from a persistent crash: here the market-wide part is netted out and the flush/no-flush split is the separator). Differences from H-0039 (funding level cross-section): conditioned on a crash day and on the change of funding during it; strict comparisons so that perps pinned at the default rate are never classed as flushed (H-0039's tie warning). Differences from H-0035: daily, not 15-minute, and conditioned on the derivatives signal, not taker share. Known risks: (a) K-0049: the rebound may be front-loaded and largely gone by the next 00:00 UTC open, which the 1-day horizon will show; (b) K-0060: the latest third of dev (bear market, serial collapses) may be negative; that is a declared kill condition; (c) timing noise: the day-t funding sum covers settlements at 00:00, 08:00 and 16:00 UTC of day t, i.e. premiums from 16:00 UTC of t-1 to 16:00 UTC of t, so a crash in the last 8 hours of day t can be misclassified as unflushed; this dilutes, it does not look ahead; (d) the flushed class may contain the larger drops on average (size confound with plain reversal), which is why both classes must already be bottom-tercile 2-sigma losers; (e) both legs can collect funding (negative funding paid to the long, positive to the short), which flatters the book slightly; (f) the BTC/ETH hedge leaves alt beta (>1) partly open, mostly offset because both sides are traded. Expected size, for the record: if flushed minus unflushed is about 1.5 % over 3 days, an event earns about 0.75 % gross side-adjusted against a round trip of roughly 25-40 bps on the event leg (perp tier), plus the hedge round trip; with a few hundred events a year at 0.10 weight this is roughly 15-25 %/y gross and well under half of that net, so the strategy needs the effect at about that size; at half of it, the book does not pass the 0.5 Sharpe bar even if the mechanism test passes. Mean gross exposure is expected around 0.3-0.5 (events on many but not all days, three-day slots, hedge). Exit on universe exit follows K-0051. Notation per perp j: r(j,t) = close-to-close return of day t; sigma(j,t) = standard deviation of daily returns over days t-30..t-1 (needs 30 valid days, else j is not eligible that day); f(j,t) = extras funding of day t (daily sum of funding rates, known after the close of t). Event candidates on day t: eligible perps other than BTCUSDT.P and ETHUSDT.P (the hedge instruments) with r(j,t) at or below the 33.3rd percentile of r(.,t) across the eligible universe that day AND r(j,t) <= -k_sigma * sigma(j,t). Classification (needs f on days t-7..t; missing funding = no event): FLUSH (side +1) if f(j,t) < 0 and f(j,t) < min(f(j,t-7..t-1)), i.e. funding turned negative and fell to a new 7-day low on the crash day. UNFLUSHED (side -1) if f(j,t) >= median(f(j,t-7..t-1)), i.e. funding did not fall at all on the crash day (strict comparisons, so coins pinned at the default rate are never FLUSH). Candidates in neither class are not events. Book: each event opens a slot at the open of t+1 with weight +0.10 (FLUSH) or -0.10 (UNFLUSHED) in that perp, held for hold_days days and closed at the open of day t+1+hold_days. A perp that has an open slot does not open a second one; a new event on a perp with an open slot is ignored. If the sum of absolute slot weights exceeds 0.5, all slot weights are scaled down proportionally to sum to 0.5. Hedge: N = sum of signed slot weights; hold -N/2 in BTCUSDT.P and -N/2 in ETHUSDT.P, so the book is dollar-neutral and gross <= 1. Weights are recomputed every day (slots expire, new slots open, hedge follows N). If a slot's perp leaves the top-30 universe or stops trading mid-hold, the slot is closed at the first decision row where it is outside the universe (no forced hold). Funding is charged/credited by the engine as usual. title: Volatility-control re-leveraging flow - tilt a 60/40 SPY/IEF book to all SPY for 2 sessions when an old large S&P day is about to leave the 20/60-session realized-vol windows

When a large daily move leaves the window, the measured volatility falls by construction, with no new information, and these funds must buy equity (futures/ETFs) and sell bonds or cash at the next rebalance (close of the session in which the window rolls, or one session later for lagged rules). The flow is large relative to closing liquidity, concentrated in one or two closes, and non-informational, so it should push large-cap US equity up relative to Treasuries over the next one to two sessions and partly give the move back afterwards. On such a date mark SPY, IVV, VTI and DIA with side +1 (large-cap US equity should outperform); IEF, TLT, SHY and AGG are never marked and serve as the same-date peers (four unmarked peers on every event date, per K-0055). Abnormal return = marked ETF return from the open of t+1 to the close of t+h minus the mean of the unmarked bond peers.","horizons":[1,2,3,5,10],"primary_horizon_days":2},"notes":"Brief fit: the brief asks for a cross-asset, 1-5 day card. This is the closest fit I could argue with a real counterparty: the signal is the S&P 500 volatility state as measured by an institutional rule (an equity-volatility estimate, not the equity price signal itself, and the event day is typically quiet), and the trade is an equity-versus-Treasury allocation, which is exactly the cross-asset trade the counterparty makes. Pure cross-market price lead-lag was killed by study mrel and macro-calendar x ETF cards by K-0065, so I did not file another of those. Family: filed under rebalancing-flow-pressure (H-0002, H-0044, H-0046) on purpose: the economic mechanism is the same (predictable, non-informational, rule-mandated stock/bond reallocation creating price pressure at the close), only the trigger differs (a volatility window roll instead of weight drift). The Chair may count it with them. It is not volatility-managed-exposure (H-0003): there the claim was a risk-return premium of timing; here vol is only the clock of someone else's forced flow, and the book's average exposure stays at the benchmark's 60/40 except on event days (K-0005, K-0027). Difference from H-0046: H-0046's breach days were large relative stock-bond move days, so generic spread reversal could not be separated. Here the trigger is the anniversary (20 or 60 sessions later) of a large day; on the event day itself nothing needs to move. Remaining confound, stated honestly: events sit in elevated-volatility regimes (a big day happened within the last 60 sessions), where the equity premium and the stock-bond spread variance are larger; the time-shifted placebo only partly controls for this. A clean control (same-regime days without a drop-out) cannot be reported by the gate. Expected numbers (rough, from typical S&P daily-return tails, not from data): with threshold 0.10 an event needs the leaving day to carry roughly a fifth or more of the 20-session squared-return sum while the 20-window binds (or an extreme day leaving the 60-window); I expect about 8-14 event dates a year, so roughly 150-250 event dates and 600-1000 marked events (4 ETFs) in 2004-2020. If the Builder's G0 count is below 50 dates or above 600 dates, something is mis-specified: please flag before G1 (K-0067). Economics (K-0064): per event the book shifts 40 % of capital SPY<-IEF and back, about 1.6 one-way legs of ETF cost (a few bps). The required margin over 60/40 is about +0.10 Sharpe, i.e. roughly 0.9 %/year at 60/40 volatility. With ~10 events a year the book needs a 2-session SPY-minus-IEF effect of roughly 25-35 bps per event; a smaller real effect will pass the mechanism test and still fail G1 (the H-0046 pattern). I state this so a G1 death after a mechanism pass is read correctly. Main risks: (1) heterogeneous rules (EWMA, other windows, multi-asset vol targets) dilute a drop-out specific flow; (2) the drop-out is known 20 sessions ahead, so desks may front-run into the close of t, before our open-of-t+1 entry; (3) the flow may be too small relative to S&P closing liquidity. Timing: SPY close at 16:00 ET; all inputs are known at the close of t; trades at the open of t+1. No references: I know no paper documenting window drop-out flows; related work on mechanical rebalancing price pressure (Harvey, Mazzoleni, Melone, 'The Unintended Consequences of Rebalancing', NBER WP 33554) and on volatility targeting performance (Moreira and Muir 2017) is a different claim, so I do not list them as the source and do not ask for the literature prior. Fixed rule constants (0.10 target, cap 1, 20/60 windows) are the industry convention, not tuned. ETFs have no forward data, so G4 is the ceiling.","signal":{"description":"Inputs: SPY daily close-to-close total return r_s = (1 + ret_co_s) * (1 + ret_oc_s) - 1 (ret_co = previous close to open, ret_oc = open to close), sessions s up to and including the close of day t. No other input. Fixed reference rule (institutional convention, not parameters): target volatility 0.10, exposure cap 1.0, windows 20 and 60 sessions, annualization 252. Step 1, at the close of day t: V20_t = mean of r_s^2 over the 20 sessions t-19..t; V60_t = mean of r_s^2 over t-59..t; sigma_t = sqrt(252 * max(V20_t, V60_t)); E_t = min(1.0, 0.10 / sigma_t). Step 2, mechanical next-session window (known at the close of t, before day t+1 trades): the session that leaves the 20-window when day t+1 is added is t-19, the one that leaves the 60-window is t-59. return were the same in every month.","why":"Some investor groups trade the same stocks in the same calendar month every year for reasons unrelated to value: year-end tax-loss selling and the January Because a stock's clientele and characteristics are persistent, the same stocks receive the same pressure in the same month each year. Heston and Sadka (2008) show that a stock's relative return in a calendar month predicts its relative return in the same month for up to twenty years; Keloharju, Linnainmaa and Nyberg (2021) show that the seasonal highs are offset by seasonal reversals in the other months, so over a year they add up to about zero: temporary, calendar-recurring mispricing, not a permanent risk premium. The time-shifted placebo moves the scores to dates whose coming calendar month is a different one, so it should earn about zero unless the result is driven by persistent stock identity.","horizons":[1,5,10,21,42],"primary_horizon_days":21},"notes":"Brief fit: the brief asks for a 1-6 month horizon in US single stocks. A calendar-month seasonality is held for exactly one month by construction (the next month is a different calendar month with a different ranking), so this sits at the lower edge of the brief; a longer hold would mix months and dilute the signal by design. Why this and not a slower anomaly: the lab's time-shifted placebo absorbs any persistent style (K-0025: low vol, profitability, value would score like their own placebos), and trend-selected events inherit their run-up in the placebo (H-0011). Seasonality is the rare cross-sectional signal whose placebo is clean: shifting the dates moves each score to the wrong calendar month, so the placebo mean should be near zero, and the score is demeaned against the stock's own other months, so persistent identity is netted out twice. That supply unlocks on fixed vesting schedules: commonly a cliff 6 to 12 months after launch, then linear monthly releases over 1 to 3 years. Every unlock gives insiders whose cost basis is near zero tokens they can sell. Retail demand at listing rests on the visible float and the listing news (the catalog itself notes that Binance lists coins after they are already popular), so it does not fully discount supply that arrives later. The claim is a slow supply overhang. Over the first year after listing, from the second month on, young coins should underperform seasoned coins of similar liquidity and beta. The effect should build roughly linearly with the holding horizon (supply arrives month by month), not sit in the first days. This is the crypto version of the long-run underperformance of new issues (Ritter 1991; Loughran and Ritter 1995). Changes from H-0004: (1) the short leg trades perps, so shorting has a real cost through funding, instead of free spot shorts; (2) the legs are sized beta-neutral, and both sides come from the same point-in-time top-30 liquidity universe, so the spread is not just high beta or illiquidity against BTC; (3) a mechanism test runs first, which H-0004 never had; (4) the horizon is set by the vesting-schedule argument (cliff at about a year), not tuned. The listing-age window is not a rescue of H-0004: the primary values are the conventional ones, and the neighbors are pre-registered. The \"longer history\" that the lesson asked for cannot be had on perps (dev 2020-2022). This is a 'cannot tell' risk the card accepts (K-0006), and the mechanism test is the main deliverable. The book rebalances weekly only to admit new listings, retire coins that come of age and keep the beta neutral. The mechanism horizon is capped at 60 days by the schema, so 60 is the primary horizon. Only the age signal is long-horizon; nothing is traded on a short-term signal. Power and cost, stated in advance (K-0053, K-0071). Round-trip cost on liquid perps is about 25-35 bps, which is negligible against a 60-day horizon, so the cost check should not bind. A near miss with the right sign in every third should be read as 'cannot tell', not as promise. Expected events: about 3-10 young coins in the top 30 on each of about 140 weekly dates, so several hundred marked events (overlapping) on well over 30 dates. Delisted pairs are only partly present in the archive, and dead young tokens are the likeliest to be missing. That biases against this card: the short leg loses its best shorts. Listing age is censored at the start of the spot data (mid-2017). This affects only coins that are seasoned in every case by 2020. The point-in-time top-30 filter means only young coins that became liquid are shorted. These are the ones with the most retail demand, which is the claimed counterparty, but also the ones with squeeze risk. Negative funding on crowded young shorts is charged by the engine. If the price effect exists but funding eats it, the mechanism test passes and the strategy fails: that answer is informative too. Study 10 found crypto short legs flipping sign between dev and holdout. This card's short leg is chosen by a structural supply variable, not by trend, but the same risk applies and G4 is the arbiter. Benedetti and Kostovetsky (ICO-era sample) report positive abnormal returns in the first 30 trading days after listing. Equal weights within a leg: each long member +G_L / |L|, each short member -G_S / |S|. All weights are reset to these targets at every weekly decision. Between decisions positions are not traded. A short coin leaves S on its own when age_j passes young_max_days, so each young coin is held short for about (young_max_days - min_age_days) days, about 11 months at the primary values. Seasoned coins stay long for as long as they are in the universe. Funding is charged by the engine (longs pay positive funding, shorts receive it, and shorts pay when funding is negative). The brief asks for a 6-24 month horizon and cross-asset signals. The signal comes from FRED macro series (interbank noon fixings), and the trades are US-listed currency trusts that also earn deposit interest. The underlying exposure is the same currency, so this is only the closest fit to \"signal from one market, trade in another\". I chose it over truly cross-asset macro timing (term spread into sectors or stocks against bonds, credit or real yields into equities) for two reasons. Second, the lab's cross-market information-diffusion claims came out flat or wrong-signed (K-0072), and Cenedese, Payne, Sarno and Valente (2016) find that equity return differentials tell little about exchange rates, so I dropped the equity-to-FX rebalancing variant. The holding horizon fits: a 5-year-average deviation changes slowly, so a currency typically stays in a leg for many months. FRED spot is used instead of the ETF prices because the ETF NAVs carry accrued interest (they would mix carry into the value score), and because FRED gives the full 5-year history before the trusts listed. Family. The value score is mechanically a long-horizon reversal of the exchange rate, so I file it under the existing long-term-reversal family (H-0060, cross-country equity ETFs) rather than a new name. The difference from H-0060: the anchor here is a fundamental one (purchasing-power parity: goods arbitrage and trade-flow adjustment), not equity overreaction, and the traded asset is the currency alone, without local equity risk. H-0060's failure is a prior against, because the FX component is part of USD country returns. That is why the card states the latest-third sign and the horizon shape as kill conditions. Persistent inflation differentials (Japan and Switzerland below the US, Australia above) bias the score: low-inflation currencies look rich because of trend appreciation that is consistent with PPP. Measuring against the trailing average, not the 5-year point change, halves that bias but does not remove it. (2) Carry is not separated. The legs earn their deposit rates through the trusts' total returns, and rich currencies can be high-yield ones, so the book may pay negative carry in overshoot phases. That is part of why the premium exists, but it means the result mixes value and carry. (3) Borrow costs of shorting currency trusts are not modelled. (4) Six instruments is little breadth. Expected numbers (K-0053, K-0064, K-0071). If the extreme-cheap minus extreme-rich spread earns a literature-sized 4-6 %/y, each side earns about 2-3 %/y against the peers, about 0.5-0.7 % per event at 60 sessions. That is several times a currency-ETF round trip (roughly 10-20 bps at these liquidity tiers). The 60-session vol of one currency against the mean of four peers is about 4 %, and picks persist across months, so effective independent windows number about 60-90. That puts the placebo 95 % bar near 0.6-0.7 %, about where the expected effect sits: a coin flip if the premium is at its literature size. A miss with the right sign, growing with the horizon and positive in every third, should be read as cannot-tell (K-0026, K-0034). The likely strategy death is the absolute Sharpe bar. ETFs have no forward data, so G4 is the ceiling.","references":[{"cite":"Rogoff (1996) The purchasing power parity puzzle, Journal of Economic Literature","year":1996},{"cite":"Asness, Moskowitz, Pedersen (2013) Value and momentum everywhere, Journal of Finance","year":2013},{"cite":"Menkhoff, Sarno, Schmeling, Schrimpf (2017) Currency value, Review of Financial Studies","year":2017}],"signal":{"description":"Inputs: FRED noon New York fixings from dataset fred_macro, keys DEXUSEU, DEXJPUS, DEXUSUK, DEXUSAL, DEXCAUS, DEXSZUS. If a currency has fewer than 90 % of the window's sessions with a fixing, or its ETF has no tradable bar at t, it is left out at that date (raise an error if fewer than 5 currencies remain; that should not happen after the period start). Long the n_per_leg currencies with the highest v and short the n_per_leg with the lowest v, each with weight +0.5/n_per_leg (long) or -0.5/n_per_leg (short), so gross = 1.0 and net = 0 (dollar-neutral: the book is a set of cross-rate positions). Weights are reset to these targets at every monthly rebalance even when the ranks did not change (small re-equalising trades). Orders are filled at the open of the next session; positions are held until the next monthly rebalance. title: Stop-cascade breakout from compressed ranges on Binance perps - follow the first taker-dominated, high-volume 15m close outside an unusually narrow 24h range, both sides, hold 6 hours

Random timing: the same trades at random times reach the 95th percentile."],"family":"stop-cascade-breakout","holding_period":{"rebalance":"event","typical_days":0.25},"market_exposure":"long_short","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Leveraged traders whose stop-loss orders and forced liquidations sit just beyond the range: they buy (sell) at market after the break, regardless of price, and pay the continuation to whoever is already positioned in the break direction. They keep doing it because tight stops near obvious levels are the standard way to cap risk on high leverage, and liquidation prices are set mechanically by margin rules.","why":"During a quiet, narrow trading range, leveraged perp traders open positions with tight stops and liquidation prices that cluster just beyond the range edges (the obvious levels). When price closes outside the range on heavy aggressive (taker) volume, those stops and the exchange's liquidation engine turn into market orders in the direction of the break. This positive-feedback flow (Osler 2005 documents it for stop-loss clusters in FX) carries price further over the following hours. The narrower the prior range relative to the instrument's own history, the more stops and liquidation levels sit close to the edge, and the more the break carries. A taker-dominated, high-volume break candle shows the cascade has started; a break on light or balanced flow is more often a drift that falls back.","why_not_arbitraged":"The payoff is per event and small in capacity (a few hours of cascade flow per instrument), false breaks are frequent so the edge only shows after costs on a selective subset, and the trade carries gap and reversal risk that market makers, who are the natural takers of the other side, avoid by widening quotes rather than by trading direction. Exchanges cannot remove the stop and liquidation clustering because it follows from leverage and margin rules."},"notes":"Brief: SCALPING, 15m Binance perps; fits the brief's 'range compression and expansion', 'forced liquidations' and 'taker-flow imbalance' directions in one rule. No mechanism_test, as the intraday judge has none. Relation to H-0035 (short-term-reversal, 15m perps): H-0035 faded 1-hour moves of 4+ sigma on 3x volume and found a front-loaded rebound. This card claims continuation on a different event set: the first break out of an unusually narrow range, and step (5) removes the H-0035 event region explicitly, so the two event sets are disjoint and the results cannot contradict each other on the same candles. The claim is that cascades are continuations at their start (breaking stop clusters) and reversals once extended; the lab has evidence only for the second half. Relation to prior studies: study 1 included daily breakout rules on US stocks and study 9 crypto trend filters on daily bars; this is intraday, conditional on compression and aggressive flow, with a hours-long hold, and it is long/short symmetric, so it does not depend on the market direction of a boom or bust year. The family name is new (stop-cascade-breakout); if the Chair considers it part of a breakout or trend-following family from study 1 or research 15 (which used the same 15m basket), the trial count should be merged. Cost arithmetic: round trip is 13 bps at the BTC/ETH tier, 16 bps at >=200M USD, 22 bps at >=50M; the top-15 in 2020 includes names in the 50-200M tier, so the card needs a mean gross of roughly 30+ bps per trade to survive doubled costs. A 6-hour move after a compressed-range break in liquid alts is typically one to a few percent in absolute size, so the claim is a modest directional edge on large moves, not a small edge on small moves. Expected trade count: about one to two qualifying breaks per instrument per month across 15 names over 36 months, i.e. several hundred to about a thousand trades; the tightest neighbor (ratio 0.5) has fewer. The failed-break exit at the range midpoint caps losses on false breaks without being a tuned stop. Thresholds in (4) and (5) are fixed round values (2x volume, 55/45 taker share, 4 sigma borrowed from H-0035), not part of the grid. Most likely death: false breaks plus costs leave the mean net trade near zero (G1), or the edge sits in the 2021 boom block (G2 sub-periods). The dev window is one boom-and-bust cycle (K-0006), so thirds are regimes.","references":[{"cite":"Osler, C. L. (2005) Stop-loss orders and price cascades in currency markets. Journal of International Money and Finance 24(2), 219-241","year":2005}],"signal":{"description":"Data: binance_perp_15m candles (o, h, l, c, qv, tbq, funding) of the point-in-time top-15 perpetuals by 30-day quote volume. Decisions after the close of every 15-minute candle t, fills at the open of candle t+1 (engine convention). Let W = range_hours * 4 candles. For each instrument j in the universe at t with at least 30 days of history: (1) Prior range: HI = max(h) and LO = min(l) over candles t-W .. t-1 (excluding t); R = (HI - LO) / c[t-1]. (2) Compression: CR = R / median of the same quantity R computed at every candle over the previous 30 days
    (2880 candles, ending at t-1). The instrument is compressed if CR <= compression_ratio.
(3) Break: long candidate if c[t] > HI, short candidate if c[t] < LO. (4) Flow confirmation (fixed, not tuned): qv[t] >= 2 x the mean qv of candles t-W .. t-1, and taker-buy share
    tbq[t]/qv[t] >= 0.55 for a long, <= 0.45 for a short.
(5) Exclusion of the H-0035 event region (fixed): skip if the absolute log return over the last 4 candles
    (c[t-4] to c[t]) exceeds 4 x the standard deviation of non-overlapping 1-hour log returns over the past
    30 days. Such moves are already-extended cascades where the lab saw a rebound, not a continuation.
(6) Cooldown: no new entry on instrument j if j had an entry in the previous W candles. Entry: a candidate that passes (2)-(6) opens a position of weight +0.25 (long) or -0.25 (short). At most 4 positions at once (gross <= 1). If more candidates than free slots arrive on the same candle, take those with the highest qv[t] / mean qv ratio; candidates that find no free slot are dropped, not queued. Exit (whichever comes first): (a) time stop after hold_hours * 4 candles; (b) failed break: a candle closes back on the other side of the range midpoint (LO + HI)/2 of the entry signal (below it for a long, above it for a short); (c) the instrument leaves the point-in-time universe (close at that decision row, per K-0051). Exits are decided at a candle close and filled at the next open like entries. No pyramiding, no reversal into the opposite side on the same candle (a new signal waits for the cooldown). Funding is charged by the engine to open positions on settlement candles. Missing candles (gap rows, real == 0) never trigger a signal; an instrument with any gap row inside the W window is skipped at t. All windows use only candles up to t.","params":{"compression_ratio":{"grid":[0.5,0.6,0.7],"value":0.6},"hold_hours":{"grid":[3,6,12],"value":6},"range_hours":{"grid":[12,24,48],"value":24}},"timeframes":["15m","1h","1d"]},"title":"Stop-cascade breakout from compressed ranges on Binance perps - follow the first taker-dominated, high-volume 15m close outside an unusually narrow 24h range, both sides, hold 6 hours","universe":{"kind":"crypto_top_n","n":15}}

title: Pre-announcement liquidity-provision reversal - LIQ-500, long 3-session losers / short winners just before their predicted 8-K earnings release, hold 5 sessions
card_json: {"asset_classes":["us_equity"],"author_agent":"scout","data_requirements":[{"dataset":"sharadar_sep","fields":["ret_co","ret_oc","dollar_volume","tradable"],"frequency":"1d","period":["2004-01-02","2020-12-31"]},{"dataset":"sec_8k_item202","description":"Real earnings-release reaction sessions; first predicted sessions exist from about 2005-08 (one year after the first filings).","fields":["ea_reaction_day"],"frequency":"event","period":["2004-08-23","2020-12-31"]}],"falsification_criteria":["Mechanism: the side-adjusted 5-session abnormal return of the events is not above the 95th percentile of the time-shifted placebos, or gross per event is below the round-trip cost (cost ratio < 1). Since H-0030 showed ordinary large-cap reversal at a fraction of cost, a cost ratio below 1 means the pre-announcement amplification is absent (or the date prediction misses) in LIQ-500.","Mechanism: the latest third of the dev events has a negative side-adjusted abnormal return (decay or regime, K-0060), even if the pooled result passes.","Mechanism shape: if the 10-session abnormal return is more than 1.5 times the 5-session one, the effect is generic slow drift rather than a concession repaid around the release, and the card's mechanism is wrong.","Strategy: net Sharpe on dev below 0.5, or below the T-bill Sharpe + 0.10, or the bootstrap bound of the Sharpe difference below zero.","Robustness: fewer than 75 % of the neighbors (formation 2/5, quantile 0.1/0.3, hold 4/6) beat T-bills, or the book's Sharpe at doubled costs does not beat T-bills.","Publication: the post-2014 part of dev earns less than half of the pre-2014 Sharpe excess."],"family":"short-term-reversal","holding_period":{"rebalance":"daily","typical_days":5},"market_exposure":"long_short","mechanism":{"counterparty":"Impatient traders who push a stock in the sessions right before its earnings release (position squaring, pre-earnings hedging and de-risking, retail positioning into the event) and must trade against thin pre-announcement depth; they pay the enlarged concession to whoever holds the other side through the release.","why":"Short-term reversal is the return to liquidity provision: market makers and other short-horizon liquidity suppliers absorb non-informational order imbalances and are paid by the subsequent price reversal (Nagel 2012). The compensation they demand rises with inventory risk. Just before a scheduled earnings release, any net position a liquidity supplier takes on will be carried through a large, unpredictable jump, so they quote less depth and require a larger price concession to absorb the same imbalance. So and Wang (2014) document that the reversal of returns over the few days before an earnings announcement, measured over the announcement window, is several times larger than the reversal in non-announcement periods. The lab already knows (H-0030, K-0044) that ordinary large-cap reversal exists but is a fraction of round-trip cost; this card claims that the pre-announcement subset is not a significance conditioner but a magnitude conditioner: the concession per event is larger by a multiple, which is exactly the gap to cost.","why_not_arbitraged":"Collecting the concession means carrying a concentrated position through the earnings jump, the very inventory risk that sets the price: market makers and stat-arb desks with risk limits on event exposure stay out or size down. The reward per unit of jump risk is modest and only diversifiable with many simultaneous names, which limits capacity and makes the trade unattractive for leveraged short-horizon capital."},"mechanism_test":{"event":"After the close of session t, a LIQ-500 stock whose predicted earnings-release session (first session on or after one of its past 8-K Item 2.02 reaction days + 364 calendar days) is exactly 3 sessions ahead, that has not had a reaction day in the last 20 sessions, and whose total return over the last 3 sessions is in the bottom quintile (side +1) or top quintile (side -1) of the LIQ-500 cross-section on that date. Unmarked peers are all other LIQ-500 members with data on the date.","horizons":[1,2,3,5,10],"primary_horizon_days":5},"notes":"Brief fit: US single stocks, cross-sectional, 5-session hold, mechanism test declared. Family: this is a short-term reversal claim (liquidity provision), so it is filed under short-term-reversal with its full trial count, not under a new name. Why it is not another 'reversal + conditioner' that K-0044 rules out: K-0044 says conditioners on the one-month sort changed significance, not size relative to cost. The pre-announcement condition is the one conditioner whose published effect is on the size of the reversal (several-fold, tied to a priced inventory risk), and the event study's cost ratio checks exactly that against H-0030's no-news reversal, which cleared the placebo but earned a fraction of cost. If this card's gross per event is still below cost, the lab can close large-cap daily reversal at the 5-session horizon for good. The date predictor (last year's reaction day + 52 weeks) is the one used by H-0023, H-0026 and H-0032; the Chair may want to count this card in the earnings-announcement-premium trials as well. Its hit rate has never been reported (K-0035); a miss dilutes the effect toward ordinary reversal, so it biases against a pass, not toward it. Helpful descriptive output if the Builder can produce it: share of events with a real ea_reaction_day in sessions P-2..P+2. The 20-session 'already released' filter uses only past data and removes known misses. Expected scale (forecast, not measured): about 500 stocks x 4 predictions a year x ~15 years, reduced by 8-K coverage gaps and the already-released filter, gives roughly 15,000-25,000 candidates and, at quintile extremes, 6,000-10,000 events on 2,000-3,500 event dates, all from 2005-08 on (first predictions one year after the 8-K data starts; no events 1998-2005). Events cluster in earnings seasons, so the book is fuller in season and light between seasons; average gross around 0.4-0.6, above the 0.20 floor. Round-trip cost for LIQ-500 names is about 6-12 bps a side pair after decimalization. So and Wang report a 3-day long-short spread of well over one percent across all stocks; the card needs roughly a fifth of that per leg in large caps (about 25-30 bps per event over 5 sessions) to clear cost by a factor of two and reach a Sharpe near the bar. The noise is high because every position is held through an earnings jump; that, not the placebo, is the most likely strategy death. Beta: losers and winners are both drawn from the extremes of the same candidate pool, so both sides carry similar volatility and the side-adjusted average is roughly beta-neutral (K-0074); there is no one-sided marked bucket. No date literals, no named stocks.","references":[{"cite":"So, E. C. and Wang, S. (2014) News-driven return reversals: Liquidity provision ahead of earnings announcements. Journal of Financial Economics 114(1), 20-35","year":2014},{"cite":"Nagel, S. (2012) Evaporating liquidity. Review of Financial Studies 25(7)","year":2012}],"signal":{"description":"Inputs: sharadar_sep daily total returns (ret_co, ret_oc), tradable flag and the point-in-time LIQ-500 membership; sec_8k_item202 field ea_reaction_day (1 on the reaction session of an earnings-release 8-K, known at the close of that session). Decisions after the close of session t using data up to that close; trades at the open of session t+1. (1) Predicted release session. For every stock j and every past reaction session L of j (ea_reaction_day == 1), the predicted next-year release session is P = the first XNYS session on or after the calendar date L + 364 days (52 weeks, same weekday). Only reaction days already observed are used, so P is known about a year in advance. (2) Candidate. Stock j is a candidate at the close of session t if t is exactly lead_sessions = 3 sessions before a predicted session P of j (t = P - 3 in session index), j is a LIQ-500 member and tradable at t, j has a total return over the formation window, and j has NO ea_reaction_day == 1 in the 20 sessions up to and including t (if the firm has already released this quarter, it is not a pre-announcement stock). (3) Formation return. r_j = compounded total return of j over the last formation_days sessions ending at the close of t (close of t - formation_days to close of t). On the same date compute the same return for every LIQ-500 member with data, and its leg_quantile and 1 - leg_quantile cross-sectional quantiles q_lo and q_hi. (4) Event and side. A candidate with r_j <= q_lo is a loser event, side +1 (expected to rebound); a candidate with r_j >= q_hi is a winner event, side -1 (expected to give back). Other candidates are ignored. (5) Book. Each event opens a slot at the open of t+1 with weight side x 0.05 of equity and is closed at the open of session t+1+hold_days (hold_days = 5, so the position spans predicted sessions P-2 .. P+2 and the reaction session if the release comes within two sessions of the prediction). Slots are fixed; no re-weighting of open slots except: if the sum of absolute weights would exceed 1.0, all slots are scaled down proportionally on that day so gross = 1.0 (no leverage). If a stock leaves the LIQ-500 universe or becomes untradable while a slot is open, the slot is closed at the first open where the engine allows it (the engine refuses weights outside the universe, K-0032/K-0051). Cash earns the T-bill rate in the engine. Missing returns in the formation window: no event. Stocks without any 8-K Item 2.02 history never become candidates.","params":{"formation_days":{"grid":[2,3,5],"value":3},"hold_days":{"grid":[4,5,6],"value":5},"leg_quantile":{"grid":[0.1,0.2,0.3],"value":0.2}},"selection_procedure":"Primary configuration fixed in advance from So and Wang's design (3-day formation, quintile extremes), with the hold set to cover a two-session error of the 52-week date prediction on either side. title: Quarter-end window-dressing cycle - LIQ-500 dollar-neutral, follow residual QTD winners minus losers in the last 10 sessions of a quarter, fade them in the first 5 of the next

This trading is driven by the reporting date, not by news, so it should (a) push quarter-to-date losers down and winners up in the final sessions of the quarter (Sias 2007: momentum profits several times larger in quarter-ending months, stronger in stocks with heavy institutional trading, i.e. large liquid names), and (b) partly reverse once the snapshot is taken and the pressure stops, in the first sessions of the new quarter (Carhart, Kaniel, Musto, Reed 2002 document quarter-end price inflation of fund holdings that reverses the next day; Ng and Wang 2004 the turn-of-the-year rebuying of losers). (2) Release entry: after the close of L, stocks in the top leg_quantile of the full-quarter RQ[L] get side -1 and the bottom leg_quantile side +1 (the pressure reverses in the new quarter). Unmarked universe members are the peers. Because the two entries sort on almost the same quarter-to-date residual with opposite sides, a generic (non-calendar) momentum or reversal effect of that sort cancels between them, and the symmetric +1/-1 marking keeps the placebo mean near zero.","horizons":[1,3,5,10],"primary_horizon_days":5},"notes":"Brief fit: US single stocks, cross-sectional LIQ-500, mechanism horizon 5 sessions. The release phase holds 5 sessions; the pressure phase holds pre_days = 10 because a release-only book would be invested about 8 % of the time and fail the 20 % exposure floor by construction (K-0027). Pressure plus release give about 15 of 63 sessions per quarter at gross 1 (mean exposure about 0.24), about 400 position entries and 3 rebalancing dates per quarter (about 235 over 2001-2020). Why this is not an old family: it is not short-term-reversal or cross-sectional-momentum in disguise. The claim is calendar-specific (only the two quarter-end windows), and the mechanism test pools a momentum-signed and a reversal-signed entry on the same residual sort, so a generic one-to-three-month momentum or reversal effect cancels in the event mean (K-0044 says those effects are small in LIQ-500 anyway); what remains is the quarter-end cycle. It is not turn-of-month-flows (H-0016, H-0025: a beta spread at every month turn driven by inflows): ranks are on beta-adjusted residual returns, so the expected beta gap between legs is near zero (K-0074), only quarter ends are used, and the pressure phase lies before the turn. Earnings contamination is small by timing: the last two weeks of a calendar quarter and its first week fall mostly before the earnings season; any post-earnings drift that is in the sort would help one phase and hurt the other and largely cancel. No 8-K, SF1 or 13F fields are needed (13F starts too late to give 30 quarter dates). Expected size (honest prior): if the large-cap quarter-end momentum premium of Sias is of the order of one to two percent per month for a quintile spread, the pressure entry should earn roughly 20-40 bps per marked stock over 5 sessions against unmarked peers and the release entry less; round-trip cost for LIQ-500 tiers is about 6-12 bps, so the cost ratio should be 1.5-3 if the cycle exists. The book turns over about 4 units of gross per quarter (enter, flip, exit), roughly 20 bps of book per quarter, so the expected net Sharpe is around 0.4-0.7: the absolute 0.5 bar is the most likely strategy death even if the mechanism passes. Fourth quarters (tax-loss selling) probably carry a disproportionate share; a G2 block check would expose a single-season effect. If a by-phase report becomes possible, please report pressure and release entries separately: a pass driven only by the pressure phase reads as quarter-end momentum, one driven only by the release phase as a turn-of-quarter reversal.","references":[{"cite":"Lakonishok, Shleifer, Thaler, Vishny (1991) Window dressing by pension fund managers. Review of Financial Studies","year":2014}],"signal":{"description":"Universe: point-in-time LIQ-500 members that are tradable on the decision day. Daily total return r[t,j] = (1 + ret_co[t,j]) * (1 + ret_oc[t,j]) - 1 (close to close). Market return m[t] = equal-weight mean of r over universe members with a return that day. Beta b[t,j] = OLS slope of r[.,j] on m over the 252 sessions ending at t (at least 200 valid pairs, otherwise the stock is not ranked). Residual quarter-to-date return RQ[t,j] = sum over the sessions s of the current calendar quarter up to and including t of (r[s,j] - b[t,j] * m[s]); a stock needs returns on at least 80 % of those sessions to be ranked. Pressure phase: after the close of E, rank ranked stocks by RQ[E,.]; go long the top leg_quantile (equal weights summing to +0.5) and short the bottom leg_quantile (equal weights summing to -0.5); fill at the open of E+1; hold these fixed target weights unchanged through the close of L. Release phase: after the close of L, re-rank by the full quarter RQ[L,.] and replace the book with the mirror: long the bottom leg_quantile (+0.5 total), short the top leg_quantile (-0.5 total), filled at the open of L+1 (the first session of the new quarter) and held unchanged for post_days sessions; after the close of session L+post_days set all weights to 0 (exit at the next open). title: Earnings-news transfer to not-yet-reporting peers - LIQ-500 long/short, follow a large 8-K release reaction in the announcer's correlated peers, hold 5 days
